title: Enterprise capacity intake: SLA benchmarking, GPU class decisioning, and scaling guidance runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a reproducible intake and prioritization runbook for enterprise dedicated capacity requests that balances SLA targets, reserved throughput commitments, and GPU class trade-offs. This doc is intended as the operational rubric product managers, solutions engineers, and dedicated-capacity SREs use during sales intake and onboarding decisions. Scope excludes pricing negotiation text and legal contract clauses; focuses on technical sizing, SLO targets, scaling guardrails, and a lightweight scoring matrix for prioritization.

Context: We see frequent enterprise asks for predictable throughput and hard latency SLOs. Mis-sized pools or ambiguous SLAs lead to cost overruns or outages. This runbook standardizes: (1) how we capture customer workload signals; (2) how we map those signals to GPU class and reserved throughput profiles; and (3) preferred scaling and fallback policies to protect production traffic and multi-tenant pools.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form collects required workload signals and quantifies 95/99 latency goals, QPS, peak tokens/sec, and concurrency
Clear mapping table from workload archetype to GPU family and quantization guidance exists and is approved by infra
Scoring rubric yields a numeric priority score (0-100) and an initial recommended reservation (GPUs and reserved TPS), with documented tradeoffs
Autoscaling templates and burst-credit rules published for three tiers: latency-critical, throughput-efficient, and best-effort
SRE and Sales have a shared checklist to confirm pre-deployment capacity verification (smoke tests, perf benchmarks, and fallback model wiring)
next_steps: Validate intake form with Solutions Eng during next three sales calls
Work with Infra to formalize GPU mapping and benchmark harness (ETA 3 sprints)
Ship an internal checklist and run tabletop for two queued enterprise customers before contract finalization
scorecard_sample: Scoring inputs: (A) Customer latency tolerance (P95/P99), (B) Sustained tokens/sec, (C) Peak concurrency, (D) Availability requirement (SLA uptime), (E) Data isolation/regulatory needs. Weighted example: A:30%, B:25%, C:15%, D:20%, E:10%. Score bands: 80-100 -> P0 onboarding (dedicated pool + high-availability), 60-79 -> P1 (reserved pool + standard HA), 40-59 -> P2 (shared pool with reservations + throttles), <40 -> P3 (self-serve guidance).
gpu_mapping: Guideline (non-normative): interactive low-latency (P95 <250ms) -> A100x or H100 with per-request KV cache and aggressive batching disabled; large-batch throughput (long context, high tokens/sec) -> H100/H800 or multi-GPU pods with quantization guidance (int8/4-bit) and larger KV caches; cost-sensitive high-throughput (best-effort latency) -> T4/RTX-class with batching and async prefix caching. Include fallback model variants: high-accuracy -> full fp16 / large model; fallback -> quantized smaller model curated per customer. Always validate with a 10-minute synthetic steady-state test and a 5-minute spike test.
scaling_policy_guidance: Templates: (1) Latency-critical: target p95 headroom 30% above baseline, vertical padding = 1.2x sustained GPUs, autoscale cooldown 60s, pre-warm pools for scheduled traffic. Burst policy: allocate burst credit up to 30% for 5 minutes, then throttle to reserved TPS. (2) Throughput-efficient: scale based on sustained tokens/sec over 3-minute window, cooldown 180s, allow spot/interruptible capacity for non-critical lanes with graceful fallback. (3) Cost-sensitive best-effort: batch aggressively, longer cooldowns, circuit-breaker at 2x baseline error rate. Include policy for cross-region fallback and model variant downgrades on sustained latency breaches.
onboarding_questionnaire: Minimum required inputs: 1) Primary use case (chat/generation/embedding/rerank), 2) Expected sustained tokens/sec and peak tokens/sec, 3) Desired p95 and p99 latency targets, 4) Concurrent sessions estimate, 5) Percent of requests requiring deterministic outputs (no sampling), 6) Data residency / isolation requirements, 7) Traffic seasonality and known traffic spike windows, 8) Acceptable fallback behavior (degrade model / queue / reject), 9) Contracted uptime SLA, 10) Any regulatory compliance needs (HIPAA, SOC2, etc).
operations_notes: Verification steps pre-provision: (1) Run canonical benchmark harness (10-minute steady-state at 80% requested throughput), (2) Validate KV cache hit uplift and cold-start latencies, (3) Execute chaos test: preempt 1 GPU from pool, observe failover latency and errors, (4) Confirm telemetry hooks and alert thresholds are in the customer dashboard. Post-deploy: daily monitoring for 72h, weekly performance review for 4 weeks.
communication_plan: For customers: provide a 3-page onboarding brief that covers recommended reservation, expected SLOs, scaling behavior, and failure modes. Internally: a single Slack channel per customer for first 30 days and a weekly sync between PM/SE/SRE until steady-state. Prepare a ticket template for runtime incidents referencing the reserved pool and the fallback model chain.
